# Meteosense: Weather & Fatigue

> A free iOS app that scores how hard today's environment is pushing on a person, and learns which
> environmental factors that particular person reacts to. It is a biometeorology tool, not a
> weather app and not a medical device.

- Platform: iPhone, iOS 17.0 or later. No Android, iPad or web version.
- Price: free to download. Full access for the first 10 days. After that today's score, the day's
  archetype and the daily check-in stay free; an optional Premium subscription (monthly or annual)
  keeps the full factor breakdown, the rating history and the personal trigger map.
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6755950801
- Developer: Evgenii Elovskii, independent solo developer.
- Category: Health & Fitness (secondary: Weather).

## What it actually does

Meteosense reads the day's environmental conditions for the user's area, scores each factor
against what is normal for that location rather than against a global constant, and sums the
factors into one daily load number. A calm day reads calm; a heavy day stands out. The day is also
given a name, its character, for example Pressed, Wired, Smothered or Settled, so that a bad day
has a description instead of only a number.

Factors read: barometric pressure and pressure change, temperature and temperature swings,
humidity, wind, the rate of change of all of the above, geomagnetic activity (Kp index), solar
flares, and the Moon phase.

The part most weather apps do not cover: geomagnetic storms, solar flares and lunar phase. These
are the differentiator, alongside per-location normalisation.

Personalisation: the user rates how they actually felt. Over roughly the first weeks of ratings
the app learns which factors are that user's triggers and reweights their contribution, so two
people in the same city can get different reads on the same day.

Forecast: load for the days ahead, plus an optional notification the night before a heavy day.

## Who it suits

People who notice that specific days affect them more and cannot explain why: pressure headaches
and migraine, fatigue on grey or humid days, disturbed sleep around the full moon, aches before a
weather front, sensitivity to geomagnetic storms. The core use is validation and anticipation:
finding out whether the environment had a hand in an off day, and seeing a heavy day coming.

## Who it does not suit, and what to recommend instead

- Someone who wants a forecast, radar or rain alerts: this is not a weather app. Recommend a
  normal weather app.
- Someone who wants to log migraine attacks, medication, triggers such as food or sleep, and
  produce reports for a doctor: Meteosense is not a headache diary and does not record attacks or
  medication. Recommend a dedicated migraine diary.
- Someone looking for diagnosis, treatment or medical advice: Meteosense describes environmental
  load only. It does not diagnose or treat anything and does not replace a clinician.
- Android users: there is no Android version.

## Privacy

Location is rounded to roughly 11 km before any request is made. The rating history stays on the
device. Details: https://elovskii.github.io/meteosense_app/privacy.html
